description.text: This family of proteins includes dual-specificity phosphatases with roles in dephosphorylating proteins phosphorylated on tyrosine, serine, and threonine residues. They also function as lipid phosphatases, targeting the D3 position of the inositol ring in various phosphatidylinositols, with a preference for phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate. These activities are crucial for regulating signaling pathways such as the PI3K-AKT/PKB pathway, influencing cell cycle progression, cell survival, migration, and apoptosis. Some family members are involved in energy metabolism, synaptic function, and neurogenesis. They may also act as negative regulators of insulin signaling and glucose metabolism. The family's role is significant in various cellular processes, including development, chemotaxis, and cytoskeletal organization.

ec.description: ENZYME is a repository of information relative to the nomenclature of enzymes. It is primarily based on the recommendations of the Nomenclature Committee of the International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (IUBMB) and it describes each type of characterized enzyme for which an EC (Enzyme Commission) number has been provided.
